subject: maths
question: A man buys 21 mangoes for a rupee. How many mangoes had he sold for a rupee so that there is a loss of 30 percent?
solution:
**Given:**

Buying price = 21 mangoes for a rupee,

Loss = 30%

**Calculation:**

For 30% loss, he has to sell all 21 mangoes in 70% of 1Rs.

Thus, SP of 21 Mangoes = 0.7 Rs

So in 1 Rs he has to sell =21/0.7 mangoes = 30 mangoes

**Hence, he had to sell around 30 mangoes for a rupee to have a loss of 30%.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] __Alternate Method__** According to the question, 

Rs. 1 = 21 Mangoes (Cost Price)

Cost price for 1 mango, 

⇒ Rs. 1/21

Now if he suffers a loss of 30%, 

Selling Price for 1 mango,

⇒ 1/21 × 7/10 = Rs. 1/30

If 1 Mango at Rs. 1/30

then he would sell 30 mangoes in Rs. 1 

**∴ He should sell 30 mangoes at Rs. 1.**
